take.text: Moodymann spins an all-Prince set at the Regent next Friday, and the following night turns into a five-way TBA-warehouse pileup — mark both.

festivals.name: Outside Lands 2026
festivals.why: Rüfüs Du Sol + The xx headline the on-taste end; Charli xcx, The Strokes, Turnstile, Empire of the Sun broaden it. ~2 months out, travel weekend. 3-day GA from ~$569.

festivals.name: Daisy Chain Fields (Olivia Rodrigo)
festivals.location: Great Park Live, Irvine (OC — ~45 mi, worth the drive)
festivals.why: Olivia Rodrigo's first festival — a one-day, all-women lineup (Chappell Roan, Doechii, Mitski, The Breeders, Bikini Kill, Garbage, Santigold + special guests Stevie Nicks, Karen O, Sarah McLachlan), 100% of net proceeds to women/girls nonprofits. Off the core house/techno lane, but a marquee must-know — and squarely on-taste for the Lori profile (she tracks Olivia Rodrigo + Mitski). Tickets via Front Gate; from $250.

festivals.name: CRSSD Festival — Fall 2026
festivals.why: SD is a drive, but this is festival-tier and on-taste — Disclosure, Chris Lake, Groove Armada (DJ set), Helena Hauff, Ben UFO, I Hate Models, Mathame, Carlita, salute. House/ techno/melodic, European lean, waterfront, 21+. NOTE: same weekend as Portola (SF) — can't do both; pick one.

festivals.name: Portola 2026
festivals.why: THE one for you — electronic-forward with DESPACIO (James Murphy + 2ManyDJs sound system), Four Tet, Soulwax, Groove Armada, DJ Shadow, Fatboy Slim, Skepta, plus Robyn, Tiësto, Swedish House Mafia. European/house energy in a warehouse-pier setting. 2-day ~$380.

festivals.name: Coachella 2027
festivals.why: Advance GA already sold out (~$549–599); lineup typically drops Sept 2026–Jan 2027. Worth tracking the lineup announce to decide if a resale is worth it.

festivals.name: GALA Festival (London) — 2027 edition
festivals.why: Quintessential European house/disco day-fest (2026: Seth Troxler, Todd Terje, Call Super, DJ Seinfeld). On-taste, but not timely — only bubble up when 2027 presale/lineup drops.

events.title: EMBRZ at Harbor House Rooftop
events.organizers: All Day All Night Events, Safra

artist_notes.name: EMBRZ
artist_notes.note: Dublin producer (Jack Casey) making atmospheric, vocal-forward melodic house — signed to Lane 8's This Never Happened label; downtempo-leaning and emotive rather than peak-time.

enrichment.curator_note: A rooftop sunset set from a This Never Happened-orbit artist is squarely the golden-hour-groove lane — EMBRZ leans dreamier and more vocal than a straight house DJ, good for the early slot rather than the whole night.
enrichment.description: Sunset rooftop set (5pm) at Harbor House DTLA with Dublin melodic-house producer EMBRZ.

verdict.why: Rooftop sunset melodic house checks the boxes but it's a single support-tier act (Lane 8's label roster, not Lane 8 himself) — pleasant, not a draw.

events.title: Midnight Lovers with Isaac Carter, Harrison BDP, Lubelski
events.detail: Focusing on feel-good house, this intimate warehouse party is a dancers-first event designed for those who appreciate close-knit crowds.

artist_notes.name: Isaac Carter
artist_notes.note: London DJ/producer, vocal-led deep house on his own Ochi imprint — championed by Ben UFO, Joy Orbison and Seth Troxler; UK-club lineage (Chicago/Detroit roots filtered through contemporary UK dance).

artist_notes.name: Lubelski
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Jake Lubell) making analog, vinyl-informed house with a wide festival footprint (Lightning in a Bottle, Desert Hearts, Dirtybird Campout) — eclectic and percussive rather than a strict selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Isaac Carter's UK deep-house pedigree (that Ben UFO/Seth Troxler co-sign carries real weight) makes this a stronger TBA-DTLA afterhours than the billing alone suggests — a legit late-night option once Harrison BDP fills in the middle.
enrichment.description: TBA-location DTLA afterhours (starts midnight) with London deep-house producer Isaac Carter, Welsh DJ Harrison BDP, and LA's Lubelski.

verdict.why: UK deep house with real cosigns — Isaac Carter is championed by Ben UFO and Seth Troxler — TBA afterhours built for the vinyl-groove lane.

events.title: Strange Case with Windows & Eighth Ball
events.detail: Keep up to date with all our upcoming events by visiting The Echo's social media and website. @theechola theecho.com

artist_notes.name: Strange Case
artist_notes.note: LA rock band, road-tested over 8+ years of SoCal gigging — KROQ 'Locals Only' airplay and a Netflix sync (The Lincoln Lawyer); dropping a new album, 'Gone For a While,' the day before this show.

enrichment.curator_note: Strange Case is a solid, road-tested SoCal rock band timing an album release show around this — a decent, unpretentious local rock bill, not something that demands a special trip.
enrichment.description: LA rock band Strange Case plays an album release show at The Echo with Windows and Eighth Ball opening.

verdict.why: Album release night at The Echo with three strong-affinity acts on the bill — exactly the small-room indie/rock lane you asked not to let electronic crowd out.

events.title: Take It Outside: Dor Wand, Things You Say x Juliet Mendoza, Xica Soul x Sonrisita, Perfect Lovers x Lovefingers, Natuta x Dick Ensalada, Masha Mar x Heidi Lawden
events.detail: Starting with live ambient before moving onto soulful house, Balearic and other head-in-the-clouds sounds, this party checks all the boxes.
reasons: +2 more like Things You Say (your pick)

artist_notes.name: Dor Wand
artist_notes.note: dublab resident (Open Heart Social Club) and Basement-affiliated ambient artist/DJ — opens sets in live ambient before shifting into soulful house and Balearic, literally this party's own format.

artist_notes.name: Xica Soul
artist_notes.note: LA selector (Daniela Zepeda) with residencies across dublab, Hyde FM and NTS — genre-spanning soulful sets moving between disco, house and everything between.

artist_notes.name: Sonrisita
artist_notes.note: dublab resident and record digger (Melissa Dueñas) behind Lowrider Sundays and the Eastside Story Project — boogie, disco and soul rooted in SoCal oldies culture.

artist_notes.name: Natuta
artist_notes.note: Tbilisi/LA DJ and co-founder of eau_de_cologne_tbs, the queer party series tied to Georgia's Bassiani club scene.

artist_notes.name: Things You Say
artist_notes.note: LA club-scene DJ project posting house mixes and playing local nights — low profile, nothing more substantial to verify.

artist_notes.name: Juliet Mendoza
artist_notes.note: 25-year LA house scene veteran, founder of Jill's House (Jackin' Jills) and a 2022 Defected Unsung Hero — dancer-rooted, deep and soulful selections.

artist_notes.name: Perfect Lovers
artist_notes.note: LA DJ (Celice Monnette) and co-founder of the Mexico City/LA queer warehouse series Por Detroit and the Muy Muy label — house and techno with a queer-community throughline.

artist_notes.name: Lovefingers
artist_notes.note: Andrew Hogge — LA-based Balearic/disco digger and 'shaman' of ESP Institute, the label/party he's run for two decades; a longtime DJ Harvey collaborator in the same cosmic-disco lineage.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based selector who co-founded Dig Deeper LA and co-runs Take It Outside itself with Heidi Lawden — cosmic disco, deep house and left-field selections.

artist_notes.name: Heidi Lawden
artist_notes.note: LA-via-London selector who cut her teeth in the '90s UK queer rave scene — house/techno/disco marathon sets, longtime DJ Harvey tour collaborator, co-runs this party with Masha Mar.

enrichment.curator_note: Masha Mar and Heidi Lawden's own day-into-night party keeps expanding — Dor Wand opening on ambient before the room turns into soulful house is exactly the arc this lane loves, and with Lovefingers, Perfect Lovers and a run of dublab regulars filling out the bill, this is worth clearing the whole Saturday for.
enrichment.description: Take It Outside's day-into-night open-air party at The Bridge, DTLA (6pm-3am), moving from live ambient into soulful house, disco and Balearic across five back-to-back pairings including co-founders Masha Mar and Heidi Lawden, Lovefingers and Perfect Lovers.

verdict.why: ESP Institute/DJ Harvey lineage day-into-night at The Bridge — Lovefingers is a two-decade Harvey collaborator, Masha Mar is core-rotation for you, and this is exactly the rooftop-vinyl-groove-into-disco arc the Sunset Sessions itch wants.

events.title: The Odyssey (70mm)
events.detail: 70MM

enrichment.curator_note: Nolan shot this entirely on Imax 70mm cameras and there are only 25 US screens that can even run the actual film print — the Vista is one of them, and demand's been pushing the run into September. Build the night around this one.
enrichment.description: Christopher Nolan's Imax-70mm Homer adaptation (Damon, Holland, Hathaway, Pattinson, Zendaya) on the big screen at the Vista.

verdict.why: Same Odyssey 70mm run as Friday — go that night instead, this is the sibling screening.

events.title: Stereo Punks & Orlove By Day Present Phantoms [Pool Party]
events.detail: Celebrate Summer with Phantoms...Poolside!

artist_notes.name: Phantoms
artist_notes.note: LA duo (Kyle Kaplan & Vinnie Pergola) making club-forward indie-dance/house — signed to ODESZA's Foreign Family Collective, praised by NPR and Billboard. More hook-driven live-electronic act than deep selector, but built for a daytime pool crowd.

enrichment.curator_note: Phantoms write bouncy, chorus-forward house-adjacent dance music that's basically made for a rooftop pool in August — not a groove-digger's set, but a legit fun daytime one if you're already DTLA that afternoon.
enrichment.description: Daytime rooftop pool party at Level 8 DTLA headlined by LA indie-dance/house duo Phantoms.

verdict.why: Phantoms (ODESZA's Foreign Family, house-meets-indie-dance) at a Level 8 pool party — hooky and radio-adjacent, but a real electronic-adjacent name in your medium tier.

events.title: Driveways
events.detail: Teragram Ballroom presents: Driveways with special guests Like Roses & Action/Adventure [August 8, 2026 / Doors 7pm / $22 advance / $25 day of show / All Ages]

artist_notes.name: Driveways
artist_notes.note: Massachusetts pop-punk trio touring on raw, hook-heavy songs like 'Fifteen Minutes' — headlining this all-ages Teragram stop.

artist_notes.name: Like Roses
artist_notes.note: Berkeley emo/pop-punk band whose 2023 single 'Easy' broke out (1M+ streams); direct support on this tour.

artist_notes.name: Action/Adventure
artist_notes.note: Touring pop-punk band rounding out the bill alongside Like Roses on this Driveways run.

enrichment.curator_note: This isn't the rooftop-house lane at all — straight all-ages pop-punk/emo — but as the live-band side of the taste goes, three real touring bands on one bill beats a single support slot as an afterthought.
enrichment.description: All-ages pop-punk/emo bill headlined by Driveways with Like Roses and Action/Adventure at Teragram Ballroom, Westlake, Sat 8/8, doors 7pm, $22-25.

verdict.why: Pop-punk/emo touring bill at Teragram — right venue, but off from your post-punk/indie/experimental rock lane.

Filming Notice: Your entry and presence on the…

verdict.why: Bobby Nsenga's deep-cuts R&B set hits the groove/soulful boost, but his actual draw is unverified.

events.title: Gimme Gimme Disco
events.detail: Live show at The Venice West: Gimme Gimme Disco.

enrichment.curator_note: This is the touring ABBA/Bee Gees/Cher dance-party circuit, DJ-hosted covers-and-hits format, not an actual disco selector's set — fine if you're already out in Venice for a sing-along, skippable if you want real crate-digging.
enrichment.description: Recurring DJ-hosted ABBA/Bee Gees/disco dance party at The Venice West bar.

verdict.why: Gimme Gimme Disco is a reliable, long-running disco dance night — hits the groove/disco taste directly.

enrichment.description: 90s house and rave classics DJ set at High Tide (9am).

verdict.why: '90s house and rave classics' is throwback programming, not a current selector set — same bucket as the decade-nostalgia penalty.

events.title: Windgrease Festival: Harmony Holiday’s Poetics of the Missing Black Notes

artist_notes.name: Harmony Holiday
artist_notes.note: LA poet, dancer, and archivist — daughter of soul singer-songwriter Jimmy Holiday, who died when she was five — whose books (Negro League Baseball, Go Find Your Father) and live performances work through jazz/soul history and Black avant-garde archives. Closer to a lecture-performance than a set.

enrichment.curator_note: Not a DJ set or a band bill — Harmony Holiday builds a live piece out of jazz history and her father's soul-music lineage, and 2220 is exactly the kind of small serious room where that actually lands.
enrichment.description: Poet and archivist Harmony Holiday presents a jazz-history performance piece as part of the Windgrease Festival at 2220 Arts + Archives (5:30pm).

verdict.why: A genuinely rare booking at a loved room, but Harmony Holiday's piece is a jazz-history lecture-performance more than a show — know that going in.

artist_notes.name: Mha Iri
artist_notes.note: Edinburgh-raised, Melbourne-forged techno DJ/producer — big-room-meets-emotional sound with her own vocals, now signed to PIAS and releasing on Adam Beyer's Drumcode; genuinely on the rise (Awakenings, Tomorrowland, Hï Ibiza in the last year).

artist_notes.name: Aundreja
artist_notes.note: LA-born, Guatemalan-American DJ on the fast rise in the local hard techno/trance scene since her 2023 debut — hypnotic, spiritual, high-BPM sets, already playing Exchange LA, Avalon and EU dates (Rex Club Paris, E1 London).

enrichment.curator_note: This is the harder, faster end of the spectrum — hard techno shading into trance, not the rooftop-groove lane — but Mha Iri's Drumcode pedigree and Aundreja's quick rise make it a legitimate booking if that's the mood.
enrichment.description: TBA-location hard techno/trance afterhours headlined by Drumcode-signed Mha Iri, with rising LA local Aundreja.

verdict.why: Mha Iri is a real rising Drumcode signee off Awakenings/Tomorrowland dates — worth the TBA-warehouse gamble even filed under hard-techno/trance.

artist_notes.name: Shonky
artist_notes.note: Paris house/tech-house lifer (Olivier Ducreux) — a third of the Apollonia trio with Dan Ghenacia and Dyed Soundorom; groovy, stripped-back underground house, well-suited to an extended set.

artist_notes.name: Silky
artist_notes.note: London house/techno DJ mentored by Frankie Knuckles — works the grey zone between deep house and techno, with releases on Culprit and My Favorite Robot.

artist_notes.name: Enzo Muro
artist_notes.note: Peruvian-born, LA-based house/techno selector and a resident of Dialogue itself — patient, flow-first sets; also co-runs the vinyl-only YouKnowWhat label/party.

artist_notes.name: Lubelski
artist_notes.note: LA producer (Jake Lubell) making analog, vinyl-informed house with a wide festival footprint (Lightning in a Bottle, Desert Hearts, Dirtybird Campout) — eclectic and percussive rather than a strict selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Shonky's extended set is the real draw — a founding third of the Apollonia crew doing groovy, stripped-back house — and Dialogue's own resident Enzo Muro plus LA's Lubelski keep the afternoon honest.
enrichment.description: Daytime dance party at DTLA's The Bridge headlined by an extended set from Paris tech-house veteran Shonky, with Silky, Enzo Muro and Lubelski.

verdict.why: Shonky's extended set plus a groove-first support bill (Enzo Muro runs his own vinyl-only label) is exactly the DTLA day-party lane you're in for.

events.title: Bears In Space Lot Party with Warehouse Preservation Society

artist_notes.name: Warehouse Preservation Society
artist_notes.note: LA disco-house DJ duo (TK & Tavish) — dynamic, acid-tinged dancefloor energy; played Glastonbury, Love International and Sunset Campout, one half rooted in '90s SF underground, the other in Venice/Ocean Park hip-hop-to-house.

artist_notes.name: Bears In Space
artist_notes.note: The LA collective behind this very party — Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez have run it since 2009, one of the city's longest-standing queer disco/house day parties, historically pulling in guests like DJ Harvey and Horse Meat Disco.

artist_notes.name: Perfect Lovers
artist_notes.note: LA DJ (Celice Monnette) and co-founder of the Mexico City/LA queer warehouse party @pordetroitmx and the Muy Muy label — house and techno with a queer-community throughline.

artist_notes.name: Stacy Christine
artist_notes.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

enrichment.curator_note: This is the real thing, not a knockoff — Bears in Space has been Silver Lake's queer disco-house day party since 2009 (DJ Harvey and Horse Meat Disco have both played it), walkable from home, and this bill is literally the people who built it — Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez themselves, plus Perfect Lovers.
enrichment.description: Bears in Space's recurring queer disco/house day party in the Akbar parking lot, with founders Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez, Warehouse Preservation Society, Perfect Lovers, and Stacy Christine.

verdict.why: Long-running queer disco day party in a Silver Lake parking lot with real pedigree (this crew has pulled DJ Harvey and Horse Meat Disco before) — solid neighborhood hang, not a headline night.

events.title: Lane 8, Sultan + Shepard, Yotto, Kasbo, Massane, Qrion, Ashibah, Grigore

artist_notes.name: Sultan + Shepard
artist_notes.note: Montreal-born, now LA-based progressive/melodic house duo (Ossama Al Sarraf & Ned Shepard) — Grammy-nominated for their Bruno Mars remix; steady, emotive mid-tempo sets since the early 2010s remix era rather than an underground name.

artist_notes.name: Kasbo
artist_notes.note: Gothenburg producer on ODESZA's Foreign Family Collective — soulful, melody-rich electronic that leans future-bass/downtempo; softer and poppier than the rest of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Massane
artist_notes.note: French melodic-house producer and guitarist — debut EP and album on Lane 8's This Never Happened, plus a release on mau5trap. Guitar-textured, emotive melodic house that sits right next to the Anjunadeep/Lane 8 end of the spectrum.

artist_notes.name: Qrion
artist_notes.note: Japan-born, Austin-based producer on Anjunadeep — shimmering, emotive melodic house; DJ Mag's 2021 Future Star, two albums deep with the label.

artist_notes.name: Ashibah
artist_notes.note: Danish-Egyptian DJ/vocalist on Defected and Get Physical — deep/tech house built around her own live vocals; more pop-house crossover than underground selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Lane 8 and Yotto anchor this fine, but it's a San Diego waterfront day-into-night — factor in the drive. The rest of the bill (Sultan + Shepard, Kasbo, Massane, Qrion) skews toward the melodic/emotive end rather than anything harder.
enrichment.description: CRSSD-affiliated melodic/progressive house day-into-night at San Diego's Waterfront Park, headlined by Lane 8 and Yotto with Sultan + Shepard, Kasbo, Massane, Qrion, Ashibah and Grigore.

verdict.why: Two tracked names (Lane 8, Yotto) headline a real CRSSD-orbit day festival — whether the SD haul is worth it is the actual judgment call here.

events.detail: This is a lineup that sits squarely on the trance into techno axis as Alan Fitzpatrick's style of big-room club debuts at WORK.

artist_notes.name: Alan Fitzpatrick
artist_notes.note: UK techno heavyweight and founder of We Are The Brave — driving, peak-time techno that tours the same circuit as Adam Beyer/Drumcode-tier bills; a legit headliner in the European techno lane.

artist_notes.name: Anastasia Giovani
artist_notes.note: SoCal-raised, now a fixture of LA's underground techno scene (SXTCY resident, founder of the VSCRL event series) — dark, textured, experimental techno sets.

artist_notes.name: Greg Downey
artist_notes.note: Belfast-born DJ/producer and founder of the Skullduggery label — started in trance (his 'Stadium' was Mixmag's Cream Ibiza anthem of 2008) before moving into deeper underground techno via his R.I.C.O alias.

enrichment.curator_note: A TBA-warehouse techno bill anchored by Alan Fitzpatrick's proper peak-time European sound, with Greg Downey's own Skullduggery imprint and LA underground regular Anastasia Giovani rounding it out — a real late one if you're up for it.
enrichment.description: TBA-location late-night techno party (WORK x Skullduggery) with Alan Fitzpatrick, Anastasia Giovani, Greg Downey, 11pm.

enrichment.curator_note: Al Green at the Hollywood Bowl is about as close to a guaranteed classic night as this city offers, and the Womack Sisters — Sam Cooke's granddaughters, dropping a Daptone debut that day — are a genuinely meaningful opener, not a placeholder.

reasons: +3 event card (+1 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Gun Outfit
artist_notes.note: Olympia-turned-LA psych/post-punk band on Post Present Medium since their 2008 debut EP — a foundational act for the label being celebrated.

artist_notes.name: The Spatulas
artist_notes.note: Bloomington, IN lo-fi punk band on the Post Present Medium roster.

artist_notes.name: Chronophage
artist_notes.note: Austin DIY punk four-piece with a sophisticated, transgressive songwriting bent — two LPs and a run of cassettes deep.

artist_notes.name: Guiding Light
artist_notes.note: Austin punk band singing bilingually in German/English over jangly, hyper-strummed garage — their debut LP just came out on Post Present Medium.

artist_notes.name: Semi Trucks
artist_notes.note: LA art-pop project fronted by Brendan Sepe, grown from a solo bedroom effort into a full band — scrappy, melodic songs.

artist_notes.name: Muscle Beach
artist_notes.note: LA four-piece delivering noisy, scattershot 'party band' improvisations — a Smell regular.

artist_notes.name: Kate Hall
artist_notes.note: No Age/Mika Miko/Dunes-adjacent LA musician (half of the News Feeds project with Luke Fischbeck & Dean Spunt) DJing the night.

enrichment.curator_note: A real DIY institution's 25th birthday at its natural home — Gun Outfit anchors a bill of scrappy touring bands (Spatulas, Chronophage, Guiding Light) that reads like a Post Present Medium family reunion, not a nostalgia cash-grab.
enrichment.description: Post Present Medium's 25th-anniversary all-ages show at The Smell: Gun Outfit, The Spatulas, Chronophage, Guiding Light, Semi Trucks, Muscle Beach, plus DJ Kate Hall, 7:30pm.

verdict.why: A real label's 25th anniversary at The Smell with its foundational act (Gun Outfit) — the DIY punk/experimental corner of the indie lane you want represented, even without a name you already track.

enrichment.curator_note: Three nights deep into Post Present Medium's 25th-anniversary run and this one's genuinely stacked — Abe Vigoda's tropical-punk reunion, Callahan & Witscher's weird new pivot into actual songs, and DIY lifers Debt Rag and reunited Portland post-punk act The Intima. events.title: Mezzanine: Rob Tregenza's Talking to Strangers (1988)

artist_notes.name: Rob Tregenza
artist_notes.note: American structuralist filmmaker — Talking to Strangers (1988) is his triple-threat debut (writer/director/cinematographer): nine unbroken 10-minute 35mm takes, shot once each, sequenced by computer-randomized order. The NYT called it an antidote to jazzy montage; a genuine formalist curio, not a normal narrative feature.

enrichment.curator_note: This is about as structurally radical as rep programming gets — nine single-take, ten-minute 35mm shots, filmed once apiece, no coverage. Not a comfortable watch, but exactly the kind of print/format-driven booking the Mezzanine series exists for.
enrichment.description: 2220 Arts + Archives' Mezzanine series screens Rob Tregenza's Talking to Strangers (1988), a formally radical nine-take 35mm feature.

verdict.why: Formalist 35mm curio (nine unbroken computer-randomized takes) at a venue you love — a real curiosity for the format-minded but too niche to build a night around.

artist_notes.name: Stacey Hotwaxx Hale

artist_notes.name: Monkey Safari
artist_notes.note: German duo (Get Physical, Anjunadeep, Bedrock) making sunny, melodic organic house — run their own Hommage label and own a club in their hometown of Halle.

artist_notes.name: Marques Wyatt
artist_notes.note: West Coast deep house legend — ran LA's long-running Deep party/residency from the late '90s into the 2010s and is generally credited with helping put LA's dance scene on the map alongside NYC and Miami.

enrichment.curator_note: Marques Wyatt basically built the LA deep house scene from the ground up, and pairing him with Monkey Safari's sunnier melodic sound for six hours under the bridge is a genuinely thoughtful booking, not just a location flex.
enrichment.description: Six-hour open-air deep house party under the 6th Street Bridge with Monkey Safari and LA scene veteran Marques Wyatt.

verdict.why: 9pm-start six-hour outdoor rave under the bridge is a night party, not a day party — and Marques Wyatt basically invented LA's deep house scene, still worth the trip for that alone.

artist_notes.note: Chicago DJ/producer (Allie DeCastris) and COSIMEA label boss — cosmic, dark, disco-inflected house/techno; a Beatport 'Next Artist' for 2025 who's shared bills with Tale of Us and CamelPhat.

artist_notes.name: Ray Kash
artist_notes.note: LA underground fixture since 2010 (Temple Tuesdays resident) — deep house into techno and melodic, weaned on Danny Tenaglia/Jonathan Peters-style New York house.

enrichment.curator_note: Afriqua alone is worth the trip to DTLA — R&S-signed, one of the more substantive deep house/techno voices around — and Azzecca/Ray Kash round it into a real groove-forward bill rather than another generic warehouse night.
enrichment.description: DTLA club date led by R&S producer Afriqua, with Chicago's Azzecca and LA local Ray Kash.

verdict.why: Afriqua's a genuinely respected R&S name — arguably the most substantive booking on the electronic slate this weekend, not just a Saturday filler DJ.

artist_notes.name: Noizu
artist_notes.note: UK-born, now LA-based tech-house producer (real name Jacob Plant) — runs his own label TECHNE Records, broke through via Chris Lake/Skrillex's HOWSLA and the platinum single 'Summer 91.' Crowd-pleasing but well-crafted house/tech-house, the mainstream end of the lane this taste explicitly wants.

enrichment.curator_note: Noizu's the kind of big-tent tech-house that earns its Spotify rotation honestly — not the deepest cut of the night but a properly good one for a bigger room like the Shrine.
enrichment.description: Tech-house DJ Noizu headlines a dance show at Shrine Expo Hall.

verdict.why: This is a tech-house club show tagged as a concert — Noizu is squarely the Chris Lake/Dom Dolla/FISHER mainstream tier you explicitly want prioritized, not background live music.

events.title: RE/FORM presents Trip To Galaxy: Joris Voorn, LUIS MIRANDA, & Materielle
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Joris Voorn
artist_notes.note: Dutch mainstay of melodic techno-house since the mid-2000s (his own Green and Rejected labels) — the 'Nobody Knows' album won Billboard's Electronic Album of the Year in 2014. Widescreen, emotive, festival-capable; not on the tracked list but a real headliner, closer to Solomun/Tale of Us than pure techno.

artist_notes.name: LUIS MIRANDA
artist_notes.note: Madrid-born, LA-based techno producer on Tronic and KD Raw — driving peak-time techno with real co-signs (Richie Hawtin, Rødhåd support his tracks); a legit local name, not filler support.

artist_notes.name: Materielle
artist_notes.note: LA techno producer/DJ steeped in '90s Detroit — dub-heavy, hypnotic, texture-first sets; still building a catalog (Delusi EPs) but a thoughtful selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Joris Voorn headlining a TBA-location night is a genuine catch — he's been putting out widescreen, emotive techno-house for two decades — and the local support here (Luis Miranda, Materielle) is real rather than an afterthought.
enrichment.description: TBA-location club night led by longtime Dutch melodic techno-house mainstay Joris Voorn, with LA techno support Luis Miranda and Materielle.

verdict.why: Joris Voorn isn't on your tracked list but plays in the exact Solomun/Tale of Us melodic-techno lane those tracked names occupy — a genuine headliner, not TBA filler.

events.title: The Fast and the Furious (25th Anniversary)

enrichment.curator_note: A 25th-anniversary big-screen Fast & Furious at the Vista is pure popcorn nostalgia rather than the arthouse rep-cinema lane, but it's the Vista and it'll be a rowdy, fun crowd for it.
enrichment.description: 25th-anniversary screening of the original Fast and the Furious at the Vista Theater.

verdict.why: Same Fast & Furious 25th-anniversary run as the 21st — go that night, this is the redundant sibling screening.

events.title: INCOGNITO presents Paolo Ferrara - LA Debut (Extended Set), Elise Ember and KriStyle

artist_notes.name: Paolo Ferrara
artist_notes.note: Italian 'Heavy Destroyer' behind TechnoMetal — hard techno fused with metal aggression and industrial noise, co-founder of the HEX movement; his 'Last Resort' hit #1 on Beatport's Hard Techno chart in 2024. A much harder, more extreme booking than the rooftop-groove lane, closer to Sara Landry's crowd.

artist_notes.name: Elise Ember
artist_notes.note: LA 'second-generation' techno DJ working the local hard/heavy techno circuit (SXTCY, Closer.LA).

artist_notes.name: KriStyle
artist_notes.note: LA hard techno/schranz DJ building a following in the local warehouse and afterhours scene.

enrichment.curator_note: Paolo Ferrara's 'TechnoMetal' is genuinely extreme — industrial-metal aggression bolted onto hard techno — so know what you're walking into; it's a real scene (HEX, Beatport #1s), just not the groove end of the spectrum.
enrichment.description: Warehouse hard techno night marking Italian TechnoMetal artist Paolo Ferrara's LA debut, with local support Elise Ember and KriStyle.

verdict.why: TechnoMetal/industrial hard techno is the harder, more extreme lane you've explicitly said isn't the draw — the 'house' tag undersells how far this is from rooftop groove.

events.title: FLOAT Rooftop Pool Party feat. Durante [2-8 PM]
events.detail: Poolside beats, curated cocktails, and skyline views above the city.

artist_notes.name: Durante
artist_notes.note: Italian-born, LA-based progressive/melodic house producer on Anjunadeep — hypnotic, groove-driven sets sitting between deep house and techno; released his debut album 'Enter' on Anjunadeep in 2024, collaborators include Amtrac and Diplo. Same melodic/Anjuna orbit as Lane 8 and Yotto.

enrichment.curator_note: A rooftop pool party with an Anjunadeep-orbit melodic house DJ is about as close to the Sunset Sessions feeling as it gets on a random weekday afternoon — this is the one to build the day around.
enrichment.description: Daytime rooftop pool party at Level 8 DTLA featuring Anjunadeep producer Durante, 2-8pm.

verdict.why: Durante's Anjunadeep pedigree puts this rooftop pool party in the same melodic lane as Lane 8/Yotto — a real daytime draw at a room you already like.

events.title: KCRW presents Latroit House Ensemble with Jason Bentley

artist_notes.name: Latroit
artist_notes.note: Dennis White — Detroit-rooted, LA-based house producer since the late '80s; won a 2018 Grammy for Best Remixed Recording on his Depeche Mode 'You Move' remix and runs the House of Latroit label/podcast.

artist_notes.name: Jason Bentley
artist_notes.note: KCRW's longtime music director and Metropolis host — a tastemaker DJ who's shaped the station's house/downtempo/global sound for decades.

enrichment.curator_note: Latroit's got real house pedigree — Detroit roots, a Grammy for that Depeche Mode remix — so pairing him with Jason Bentley's KCRW ear reads like a legit live-house-band show, not a DJ-booth filler slot.
enrichment.description: KCRW's Jason Bentley joins Grammy-winning house producer Latroit's live ensemble at Say Yes.

verdict.why: A Grammy-winning house producer's live ensemble with KCRW's Jason Bentley is a more interesting format than a straight DJ set.

enrichment.curator_note: Koletzki's been doing the big-room-but-emotive melodic house thing since before it was a genre label — a solid, reliable pick if you want groove without going full techno.

events.title: Haddaway, Ultra Naté, Robin S, Crystal Waters & More
reasons: +4 event card (+3 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Ultra Naté
artist_notes.note: Baltimore club/house vocalist behind '90s anthem 'Free' — a real voice of that Yoshitoshi/Deep Dish-adjacent house era, not a manufactured pop act.

artist_notes.name: Crystal Waters
artist_notes.note: NYC deep-house vocalist — 'Gypsy Woman (She's Homeless)' and '100% Pure Love,' both Basement Boys productions, are genuine foundational house-anthem catalog.

artist_notes.name: Robin S
artist_notes.note: UK house vocalist whose 'Show Me Love' (1993) is one of the most sampled/replayed piano-house records ever — a real genre landmark even if the name itself isn't a household one.

enrichment.curator_note: This is a house-legends day party, not a tribute act — Haddaway, Ultra Naté, Robin S and Crystal Waters all made the actual records, so a free outdoor DTLA stage is a genuinely good way to hear 'Show Me Love' and 'Gypsy Woman' from the people who made them.
enrichment.description: Outdoor '90s house-classics day party at Pershing Square with original vocalists Haddaway, Ultra Naté, Robin S and Crystal Waters.

verdict.why: These are the actual original house vocalists behind genuine genre landmarks (Robin S, Crystal Waters), not a tribute act — an outdoor day party built on real catalog, not nostalgia karaoke.

enrichment.curator_note: Setaoc Mass alone is a real European-caliber techno booking — Berghain/Bassiani-level hypnotic techno — and pairing him with NYC veteran Adam X and LA's own Marie Nyx makes the TBA-address afterhours format worth the gamble.

artist_notes.note: Atlanta producer/DJ blending techno, electro, breaks and UK bass into something genre-agnostic and physical — releases on Dirtybird and Lobster Theremin, mentored early by Underground Resistance's Mike Banks.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — Italo disco, house and dancefloor edits.

artist_notes.name: Tottie
artist_notes.note: Dublab-affiliated LA radio host and co-founder of SOS Music, a !K7-backed label/platform spotlighting women and non-binary electronic artists.

artist_notes.name: Stacy Christine
artist_notes.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

enrichment.description: Studio Barnhus summer day party with Axel Boman, Kornél Kovács, and Nikki Nair at The Bridge (5pm).

verdict.why: Masha Mar is a core artist in your own listening data, and Axel Boman/Kornel Kovacs are internationally respected underground house names — the score plateaued at 8 but this is the real headline of the weekend.

events.title: DJ Susan POOL PARTY at Level 8 [Labor Day Saturday]
events.detail: Celebrate Labor Day Weekend with DJ Susan...Poolside!

artist_notes.name: DJ Susan
artist_notes.note: Alias of Steven Glathe (Hood Politics Records, San Diego) — bass/tech-house built for big builds and gritty drops, several Beatport #1s. More festival-EDM energy than a groove selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Labor Day rooftop pool party checks the setting boxes (near home, Saturday, open-air), but DJ Susan is a build-and-drop bass-house guy, not a digger — go for the pool and the day-drinking, not a deep set.
enrichment.description: Labor Day Saturday daytime pool party (2-8pm) at Level 8's rooftop deck headlined by bass/tech-house DJ Susan.

verdict.why: Scene notes peg DJ Susan as festival-EDM bass-house built for big drops, not a groove selector — the pool setting doesn't save a booking that's off-lane.

artist_notes.note: Italian-born, Berlin-based DJ/producer with residencies at Berghain/Basement — Chicago house, Italo-disco and electro-disco worked through analog '70s/'80s hardware; a genuine Live at Robert Johnson / Ostgut Ton pedigree, deeply in the European lane.

artist_notes.name: James Axon
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ (dublab resident, 'Hearing Color') and founder of the queer underground party Planet Love — deep house, dreamy techno, Italo, Balearic and psych-disco; a real musician's ear (former pianist), has played alongside Octo Octa, Eris Drew, Derrick Carter.

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — Italo disco, house and dancefloor edits.

enrichment.curator_note: Massimiliano Pagliara headlining Midnight Lovers is a legitimate European-club booking — Berghain-lineage electro-disco with Masha Mar and James Axon rounding it out with LA's own deep-house/dublab crowd. This is the kind of night the fabric-London comparison is actually built for.

events.title: Âme, DJ Tennis, Kaz James - Chinatown Block Party
reasons: +4 event card (+2 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

sounds_like: Life and Death's soulful, post-rock-tinged house

artist_notes.name: DJ Tennis
artist_notes.note: Manfredi Romano — Italian scene godfather who founded Life and Death in 2010 (Tale Of Us, Mind Against and Carlita all came up through the label); a globally touring, melodic house/techno selector with real ties to the Innervisions crowd via the Rakastella festival.

artist_notes.name: Kaz James
artist_notes.note: Australian DJ/producer with old-school pedigree — a decade-long Pacha Ibiza residency (Nic Fanciulli's 'We Are The Night') behind him, now making straight-up house that's charted with tracks like 'Not in Love' and 'Footprints.'

artist_notes.name: Masha Mar
artist_notes.note: Serbian-born, LA-based DJ/curator (the Midnight Lovers crew) with NTS and Dublab residencies — Italo disco, house and dancefloor edits.

enrichment.curator_note: Âme running an actual outdoor Chinatown block party — not a warehouse pop-up or a festival stage — is exactly the kind of booking worth clearing a Saturday for; DJ Tennis and Masha Mar rounding out the bill only sweetens it.
enrichment.description: Outdoor block party on Gin Ling Way in Chinatown headlined by Innervisions co-founder Âme, with Life and Death's DJ Tennis, plus Kaz James and Masha Mar.

events.title: FLOAT Rooftop Pool Party feat. Apache [2-8 PM]
events.detail: Poolside beats, curated cocktails, and skyline views above the city.

artist_notes.name: Apache
artist_notes.note: Miami-based, French-born DJ/producer on Abracadabra Records (Miami house/techno label) and founder of the Soundtuary party series — warm, groove-driven house suited to a rooftop-pool crowd.

enrichment.curator_note: A genuine rooftop-pool day party — Apache isn't a name you'll recognize, but Abracadabra's house lane is legit groove, not brostep-adjacent EDM, and the setting alone (2-8pm, DTLA rooftop) is the Sunset-Sessions kind of afternoon you like.
enrichment.description: Daytime rooftop pool party (2-8pm) at Level 8 DTLA headlined by Miami house DJ Apache.

artist_notes.name: DRAMA
artist_notes.note: Chicago R&B/dance duo — producer Na'el Shehade and vocalist Via Rosa — genre-blurring pop/dance/jazz songwriting; played Coachella alongside Frank Ocean and Gorillaz.

enrichment.curator_note: Sofi Tukker at the Greek is a Spotify-core-rotation lock, not a discovery pick — a fun big-room night if you're already a fan, and DRAMA's a genuinely tasteful opener rather than filler.
enrichment.description: Sofi Tukker headlines the Greek Theatre with support from DRAMA, 7:30pm.

artist_notes.name: Chemtrail Johnny

artist_notes.name: Hazy
artist_notes.note: Recurring Sunday Sessions LA resident — vinyl-only house sets, a regular on the rotation at the series' open-airs.

artist_notes.name: Ian Llorens
artist_notes.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

artist_notes.name: Gilbert0
artist_notes.note: Another Certified Groovers regular — same all-vinyl deep-house lane, secret-location DTLA parties.

enrichment.curator_note: Certified Groovers landing Gene On Earth is a nice get — his Limousine Dream sound is more minimal-and-breaks-leaning than most of the TBA-warehouse bills this month, worth it if you want something a shade weirder than straight house.

artist_notes.note: Detroit DJ/producer (Ariel Corley) blending house, disco, Motown, and techno — 2025 debut album 'House In The Dark' leans into Afrofuturism; praised by Carl Craig and The Blessed Madonna, has played Panorama Bar and Smart Bar.

artist_notes.name: Colored Craig
artist_notes.note: LA DJ known for soul/funk/jack-leaning house sets — a regular guest at A Club Called Rhonda over the years.

artist_notes.name: Goddollars
artist_notes.note: LA-born (Loren Granich), co-creator and resident DJ of A Club Called Rhonda — has held down all-vinyl disco sets there with partner Paradise for over a decade.

artist_notes.name: Gay Felony
artist_notes.note: LA DJ/producer (Melody Scallion) — extended vinyl sets ranging from soulful/progressive house to hard house and melodic techno; hosts a Dublab radio show.

artist_notes.name: Anastazja
artist_notes.note: LA-based DJ (USC grad) who came up through Soulection Radio, played Boiler Room, and recently supported Keinemusik's Rampa — a credential that tracks with the melodic/Keinemusik lane.

artist_notes.name: DJ Minx
artist_notes.note: Detroit house matriarch, Women on Wax founder — tracked artist; deep, soulful, dancefloor-first selection.

artist_notes.name: A Club Called Rhonda
artist_notes.note: LA's own queer disco/house institution (Loren Granic & Gregory Alexander) — the closest thing on this bill to the rooftop-groove lane, all disco edits and drag-flecked chaos rather than a band.

enrichment.curator_note: A Club Called Rhonda is one of the last real queer dance institutions left in LA, and stacking Detroit's DJ Holographic next to their own deep bench of residents (Goddollars, Gay Felony, Colored Craig) plus DJ Minx makes this one of the stronger bills on the whole calendar, not just a queer-night box to check.
enrichment.description: Long-running LA queer club night A Club Called Rhonda at Los Globos, with Detroit house veterans DJ Minx and DJ Holographic plus a deep bill of LA residents.

verdict.why: Amelie Lens solo at Grand Park via Factory 93 — outdoor block-party format, legit promoter, tracked headliner. September date gives time to plan; the RA pick confirms it's already on radar.

reasons: +4 event card (+3 draw, +1 rare booking, +1 stacked bill)

artist_notes.name: Floorplan
artist_notes.note: Robert Hood & daughter Lyric Hood — Detroit techno royalty (M-Plant) turned deep, gospel-inflected house. 'Baby Baby' fills a floor for a reason.

artist_notes.name: HoneyLuv
artist_notes.note: Cleveland-born, ex-Navy — one of the biggest tech-house breakouts of the last few years; soulful, groovy end of the genre, runs her own 4 Tha Luv label.

artist_notes.name: Hannah Laing
artist_notes.note: Dundee DJ, ex-dental technician turned fast-rising UK name — high-energy trance and hard house, runs the doof label and just launched her own festival.

artist_notes.name: Coco & Breezy
artist_notes.note: Twin sisters (also the eyewear-brand founders) turned house/dance DJ duo — danceable, R&B-tinged, more crossover-pop energy than underground.

artist_notes.name: STRAWBRY
artist_notes.note: LA underground fixture (South Florida-raised) — breaks-and-house sets, runs the STUDIO5400 party series.

artist_notes.name: Vieze Asbak
artist_notes.note: Dutch 'memecore'/troll-rave artist out of Amsterdam's Pestcore Collectief — hard-dance-adjacent chaos, not clean house or techno. A sign this bill gets weird in spots.

artist_notes.name: Jazzy (IRL)
artist_notes.note: Couldn't pin down a confident bio for this one — flagging as unverified rather than guessing.

enrichment.curator_note: Boiler Room's Sunday day party stacks Floorplan's gospel house and HoneyLuv's tech-house heat against Hannah Laing's hard-house hype and a Dutch memecore act, with several names even RA barely has bios for — genuinely one of the most eclectic single-day bills on the radar, go in expecting variety over consistency.
enrichment.description: Boiler Room's LA day party (venue TBA) — a 14-act, multi-genre bill headlined by Floorplan, HoneyLuv, and Hannah Laing.

events.title: The Outsiders (Touring)
events.detail: The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.Adapted from S.E. HINTON’s seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA’s iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) and Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, and arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, and direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation."In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self- discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging…and the realization that there is still “lots of good in the world.”

events.title: Bonnie Raitt: Live 2026 with Special Guest Jon Cleary
lineup: Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen
events.detail: Bluesy singer/songwriter Bonnie Raitt has worked long and hard for her multiple Grammy Awards, hit singles and chart-topping records. Since her 1971 eponymous debut, the California-born performer and long-time activist has steadily maintained a music career, albeit with definite peaks and valleys. The red-headed songstress, one of the only women of her time to play guitar using the bottleneck technique, unleashed seven albums in just nine years, though her big commercial break came with her 10th studio set, 1989’s “Nick of Time.” That 11-track collection, produced by Don Was, earned three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. Not only has the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer tackled multiple U.S. tours and international runs, but she’s also a frequent participant in events of social activism, such as Farm Aid and Amnesty International concerts. Raitt’s 16th full-length album and most recent studio release, “Slipstream,” hit retailers in 2012. Not only did ticket sales for the support tour soar, but Raitt also landed the best-selling blues album of the year and took home the Grammy for Best Americana Album.

profile.taste_yaml:
# Taste profile — the taste CONTENT. Edit freely; every run re-reads this.
#
# Since Track B (2026-07, LLM-first ranking): the event-editor LLM is the RANKER — this whole
# file rides in its judging brief (categories/boosts/penalties/tracked/narrative), and the
# keyword weights below act only as a coarse pre-filter + within-tier tiebreak. Don't hand-tune
# the numbers for ranking effect anymore; say what you like in words (here or via the concierge)
# and the editor applies it.

# The narrative — the taste in prose. This is the highest-signal part of the editor's brief;
# keep it current as your taste moves.
narrative: >
  Curated as an electronic head: the spine is house / techno / tech-house across
  the spectrum — from rooftop-vinyl-groove and proper European club nights all
  the way to mainstream festival/big-room headliners (Chris Lake, FISHER, etc.
  ARE priority, not noise). A recurring favorite — one kind of event he likes,
  not the be-all: "Sunset Sessions at Golden Hour DTLA" — chill rooftop, vinyl,
  house, European feel. But don't let "tasteful" exclude the big fun mainstream
  sets. Film is a real lane, not filler: a rep/arthouse regular (Vidiots, Vista,
  New Bev, Cinematheque) where the format is part of the draw — 70mm/35mm
  prints, restorations, Q&As — and a director-event (Nolan, PTA, Tarantino,
  Lynch tier) is worth building a night around; judge the movie and the print,
  not just the room (see the `film:` block).

categories:
  high:
    # weight +3 each match
    - house / techno / tech-house / acid / electro / minimal / melodic — DJ sets
      of all sizes
    - mainstream & festival-scale house / tech-house headliners (John Summit,
      Dom Dolla, Gorgon City, etc.) — big-room fun counts, not just the
      underground
    - fabric-London-style proper club nights / European-leaning dance lineups
    - rooftop / sunset / daytime open-air house, disco, Balearic, groove sets
    - vinyl-only / all-vinyl / listening-bar DJ sets
    - warehouse and afterhours parties (incl. location-TBA)
    - melodic/organic/afro house + progressive
      (Anjuna/Innervisions/Keinemusik/Afterlife orbit)
    - rep & arthouse cinema (Vidiots, Vista, Brain Dead, Cinematheque, New Bev)
    - small rock / indie band shows at clubs (Troubadour, Echo, Zebulon,
      Moroccan, Lodge Room, Teragram) — post-punk, indie, garage, dream-pop,
      experimental, krautrock-y
    - Goldenvoice events
  medium:
    # weight +2
    - live electronic / electronic-adjacent acts (Rüfüs Du Sol, ODESZA, Bonobo,
      Jamie xx tier)
    - daytime & lifestyle — flea / vintage / design markets (Rose Bowl Flea,
      Melrose Trading Post), farmers markets (esp. Silver Lake/eastside), food &
      drink pop-ups, brand activations / block parties / spritz-type parties,
      neighborhood street fairs
    - record fairs, listening bars, food events with a music angle
    - craft beer events / brewery takeovers / festivals
    - theater (Pantages-scale and black-box)
    - concerts of big name artists (Kendrick Lamar, Kacey Musgraves, Tame
      Impala) — mostly to stay informed
  low:
    # weight +1, include only if exceptional
    - standup comedy — NOT generally wanted; only known/favorite names (see
      comedians_loved)

boosts:
  # +1 each (stack)
  - rooftop / open-air / sunset / golden-hour setting
  - vinyl-only or "all night long" / open-to-close single-DJ sets
  - European vibe/feel — UK/EU DJs, labels (fabric, Rush Hour, Running Back,
    Defected, Hot Creations, Innervisions, Keinemusik) / Balearic-disco
  - groove / soulful / deep / dub / disco-leaning house
  - lineup artist in artists_tracked (also gets a "tracked" badge; effectively
    +2 via the list)
  - walkable or short drive from Silver Lake (Hyperion & Del Mar)
  - Friday or Saturday night
  - independent editorial mention (LAist, Time Out, DiscoverLA, 6AM, Dirty Epic)
    — +1 per source
  - RA pick flag
  - early-bird ticket tier still available / on-sale or selling fast
  - headliner / big-name act in a small or intimate venue

penalties:
  # -2 each (the expanded non-priority list)
  - Vegas-style bottle-service / table-service clubs (Hakkasan/Marquee energy)
  - generic Top-40 / open-format / hip-hop "club night" with no real DJ billing
  - hardstyle / gabber / happy-hardcore / hard-dance as the main draw (not the
    lane)
  - dubstep / riddim / bass-music mega-shows, brostep
  - 18+ EDM mega-raves built on production over selection
  - tribute / cover bands, "[decade] night" nostalgia club nights
  - sports-bar watch parties, trivia, open-mics, networking mixers, webinars
    (World Cup etc. belongs in "Around town," not the picks)
  - country, Christian, kids/family programming
  - far-flung (Temecula / Anaheim / OC / SD / Ventura / SF) unless genuinely
    worth the trip
  - Coachella-tier logistics without Coachella-tier payoff
  - drag show
  - drag revue
  - cabaret

# Tracked artists — match in a lineup => +2 and a "tracked" badge. Curated across the spectrum;
# grow this as you react. (Underground/European → mainstream tech-house → techno → live.)
artists_tracked:

  # mainstream / festival tech-house & house (priority too)

  ] # +1

# Film taste — the MOVIE, not just the theater (venues_loved already boosts the Vista etc.).
# Deterministic layer: directors_tracked = +2 per match (like artists_tracked), formats_loved =
# +1 per match (the print/format draw — a 70mm title tag beats a stream). Gated to film-typed
# events. The event-editor also reads this whole block in its brief, so the LLM layer can weigh
# what it KNOWS about a film (director, rep-canon status, restoration buzz) even when the
# listing text doesn't say it. SEEDED from the rep/arthouse line above — edit freely.
film:
  directors_tracked:
    - Christopher Nolan
    - Paul Thomas Anderson
    - Quentin Tarantino
    - David Lynch
    - Denis Villeneuve
  formats_loved: [ 70mm, 35mm, 16mm, nitrate ]

# Feedback log — append reactions here ("more like X", "never show Y");
# periodically fold them into the weights above.
feedback:
  - "2026-06-16: rooftop vinyl house w/ European feel is a core lane; Sunset
    Sessions is one example (don't overstate it)."
  - "2026-06-16: techno + house both mainstream and underground (fabric-London
    energy)."
  - "2026-06-16: not a comedy fan generally; surface known names only (loves
    Stavros Halkias)."
  - "2026-06-16: surface Sunset Sessions @ Level 8 when it's on — a recurring
    favorite / one kind of event I like (not a headline)."
  - "2026-06-16: festival radar should be compact + urgency-driven, not a
    curated list dump."
  - "2026-06-16: mainstream big-room headliners (John Summit et al.) ARE
    priority too — don't down-rank them as 'mainstream EDM'. Curate like an
    electronic head."
  - "2026-06-16: surface the live-band lane too (indie/rock/experimental —
    Zebulon, Troubadour, Echo, Moroccan, Lodge Room, Teragram); don't let
    electronic crowd it out of the digest. NOTE: Zebulon is JS-rendered and
    currently uncaptured (e.g. Mamas Gun) — needs a real fetcher."
  - "2026-07-20: Boost big-name acts booked in small/intimate venues (\"big name
    in a place you wouldn't expect\"). (self-edit via concierge)"
  - "2026-08-02: Down-rank drag / cabaret performance events (self-edit via
    concierge)"
profile.profile_yaml:
# profile.yaml — place + person *infrastructure* config for the scoring engine and fetchers.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lifted out of Python (the term lists + geo in build_dashboard.py, the dma/area ids in the
# fetchers) so the engine is city/person-configurable and the scoring logic can live in ONE
# place: scripts/lib/scoring.py. Split of concerns:
#   taste.yaml  = CONTENT  — what Ari likes (artists_tracked, venues_loved, lanes)
#   profile.yaml = MECHANISM — source ids, home/geo, scoring weights, term matchers, thresholds
# Change city/person by swapping this file; the scoring code doesn't change.
# Values below are transcribed verbatim from the pre-refactor build_dashboard.py (behavior-preserving).

city: Los Angeles
timezone: America/Los_Angeles

# Home base — drives the "close to home" boost and the night-planner's travel times.
home:
  neighborhood: Silver Lake
  cross_streets: Hyperion & Del Mar
  coords: [ 34.0906, -118.2717 ] # ~Hyperion & Del Mar; used by scripts/lib/geo.py

# City-specific source ids (lifted from the fetchers; they fall back to these literals).
dashboard:
  # Page-presentation knobs (the static dashboard reads these via feed config).
  # photos: real event images on the front page's top picks (lead + shortlist) for
  # signed-in profiles. Default false — flip here (or preview via the owner's in-page
  # Settings toggle) to turn them on site-wide at the next feed build.
  photos: false
  # Public URL of the deployed dashboard. Digest event lines add a `card ↗` link to
  # <site_url>?e=<event_key>, which opens that event's card (details + save) on the site.
  # Blank/absent = digests carry ticket links only.
  site_url: https://arinazari.github.io/la-events/

sources:
  ticketmaster_dma_id: "324" # LA DMA — fetch_ticketmaster.py
  ra_area_id: 23 # RA's internal LA area number — fetch_ra.py
  # Beatportal (Beatport Tickets) geo filter — fetch_beatport.py; their own LA preset.
  beatportal_city:
    city_name: Los Angeles
    country_code: US
    radius: "100"

pipeline:
  # Out-of-market drop (Ari, 2026-07-17): TM's DMA 324 reaches Palm Springs / Paso Robles /
  # SD-adjacent venues; rows whose neighborhood is listed here are dropped at merge time
  # UNLESS radar-worthy (festival title / tracked artist / arena-tier venue — so Coachella,
  # a tracked name at Pappy's, or a Yaamava headliner still gets captured). This is the
  # >~80-mile line; day-trip far (Anaheim/OC/Riverside/Ventura/Ojai) stays in-catalog and is
  # handled by the far scoring penalty instead. Edit freely — it's policy, not code.
  out_of_market:
    - palm springs
    - rancho mirage
    - palm desert
    - cabazon
    - coachella
    - indio
    - pioneertown # Pappy & Harriet's — tracked/festival bookings survive via the radar door
    - yucaipa
    - san bernardino
    - highland # Yaamava sits here — its arena headliners survive via the radar door
    - san diego
    - santa barbara
    - paso robles
    - san luis obispo
    - bakersfield
    - palmdale
    - temecula
    # out-of-state junk that occasionally rides in via TM/Eventbrite fetcher noise:
    - bolingbrook
    - portland
    - sunrise

scoring:
  # Base category weight, mirroring taste.yaml high/medium/low. Comedy is special-cased in code
  # (suppressed unless a loved comedian). Unknown categories default to 1.
  category_weights:
    electronic: 3
    party: 3
    film: 1
    music: 2
    live_music: 3
    theater: 2
    beer_food: 2
    comedy: 1
    art: 1
    pop: 1
    general: 1

  # Raw-score -> 1..5 star rating. [min_score, rating], checked high-to-low; below all => 1.
  rating_thresholds:
    - [ 8, 5 ]
    - [ 6, 4 ]
    - [ 4, 3 ]
    - [ 2, 2 ]

  # Neighborhoods walkable / a short drive from home (+1). Matched case-insensitively.
  near_home_neighborhoods:
    - silver lake
    - silverlake
    - echo park
    - los feliz
    - east hollywood
    - atwater village
    - atwater
    - frogtown
    - elysian valley
    - highland park
    - eagle rock
    - glassell park
    - cypress park
    - lincoln heights
    - chinatown
    - virgil village
    - westlake
    - historic filipinotown
    - downtown
    - dtla
    - arts district

  # +1: rooftop / vinyl / groove setting.
  groove_terms:
    - vinyl
    - all night
    - open to close
    - open-to-close
    - groove
    - disco
    - soulful
    - deep house
    - balearic
    - rooftop
    - sunset
    - golden hour
    - open-air
    - open air
    - daytime
    - day party
    - poolside
    - pool party
    - beach
    - small venue
    - intimate
    - club show

  # +1: European label / vibe.
  eu_terms:
    - fabric
    - defected
    - innervisions
    - keinemusik
    - hot creations
    - rush hour
    - running back
    - anjuna
    - afterlife
    - dirtybird
    - hot since
    - solid grooves

  # -2 each distinct term: the expanded non-priority list (off-taste programming).
  penalty_terms:
    - bottle service
    - bottle-service
    - vip table
    - table service
    - top 40
    - top-40
    - open format
    - open-format
    - hip hop
    - hip-hop
    - hardstyle
    - gabber
    - dubstep

    - watch party

    - sports bar

    - open mic
    - karaoke
    - networking
    - webinar
    - workshop
    - virtual
    - zoom
    - mega-rave
    - mega rave
    - edm festival

  # -2: far-flung (not worth the trip by default).
  far_terms:
    - anaheim
    - santa ana
    - irvine
    - san diego
    - temecula
    - ventura
    - riverside
    - long beach
    - costa mesa
    - huntington beach
    - paso robles
    - laguna beach
    - rancho mirage
    - palm springs
    - san bernardino
    - bakersfield

  # Spotify + feedback music layer (Phase C). The affinity artifact
  # (data/spotify_affinity.json) is built by scripts/fetch_spotify.py from top/followed/
  # recently-played and folded with the feedback log; the scorer turns it into points here.
  # Spotify ENRICHES taste.yaml — it never overwrites it. Tune freely; all optional.
  spotify:
    # Points an affinity artist contributes when it appears in a lineup/title, by tier.
    # `hidden` = a feedback "never show" down-rank.
    tier_points:
      core: 3 # long-term top / followed / multi-signal — your spine; reliably clears ★4
      strong: 2 # heavy rotation — a real nudge above "on rotation"
      light: 1 # on rotation — a gentle bump
      hidden: -3 # feedback: never show this artist
    artist_cap: 5
      # max total artist-affinity points per event (a core + a strong both register;
      # a stacked dream lineup still can't run away)
    genre_points: 1 # points when a high-affinity Spotify genre appears in the haystack
    genre_threshold: 0.5 # min normalized (0..1) genre affinity to count
    genre_cap: 1 # max genre points per event (kept conservative — genre match on free text is noisy)
    min_name_len: 3 # skip ultra-short artist names (avoid false substring matches)
    # Single-word artist names that are also common English/party words or surnames (the band
    # Train, the rapper Future, the tech-house FISHER). These only count when they match a
    # structured lineup ENTRY, never loose title text — shared by the Spotify layer AND the
    # tracked-artist/radar matchers (Track B3: 'Fisher and Thames' must not badge FISHER,
    # 'The Drama' must not badge DRAMA). Grow this as you spot more.
    ambiguous_names:
      [
        train,
        future,
        juice,
        jungle,
        lights,
        justice,
        work,
        sanctuary,
        paradise,
        chance,
        hold,
        alive,
        fisher,
        drama
      ]

  # Feedback loop (Phase C). Reactions in data/feedback.jsonl fold into the affinity layer
  # automatically (no hand-merge into taste.yaml). Each weight nudges an artist/genre; once
  # the summed weight clears affinity's tier thresholds it scores like a Spotify artist.
  feedback:
    weights:
      loved: 2.0 # "more like this"
      went: 1.5 # you went
      clicked_ticket: 0.5 # implicit — emitted by the digest/dashboard delivery surfaces (Phase B/D)
      added_calendar: 0.5 # implicit — ICS export / save-to-calendar
      skipped: -0.5 # soft down-nudge
      hide: -10.0 # "never show" — forces the `hidden` tier (hard down-rank)

# Travel / geography for the night-planner (scripts/lib/geo.py). Used to sequence
# dinner -> show -> afters with rough drive/walk times. The LA neighborhood-centroid
# and venue->neighborhood gazetteers are code defaults in geo.py (same idiom as the
# scoring term-lists); override or extend them here per city/person. Only the tunable
# `travel` knobs live here by default — add `neighborhoods:` / `venues:` to override.
geo:
  travel:
    walk_max_miles: 0.8 # at/under this straight-line distance, prefer walking
    walk_min_per_mile: 20.0 # ~3 mph
    drive_floor_min: 8 # any drive costs at least this (parking, getting going)
    park_buffer_min: 6 # find parking + walk from the car
    short_min_per_mile: 4.0 # surface streets w/ lights (~15 mph effective)
    long_min_per_mile: 2.4 # some freeway on longer hops (~25 mph effective)
    short_threshold_miles: 4 # beyond this, the tail is freeway-paced
  # neighborhoods:             # uncomment to override geo.py's LA centroids
  #   Silver Lake: [34.0869, -118.2702]
  # venues:                    # uncomment to map venues -> neighborhood for blank/city-level records
  #   Zebulon: Frogtown
